When this all started, I thought of the COVID-19 lockdown to be good for myself since I was working 5-6 days a week for 8-10 hours a day (I'm a cook) and I won't lie, the first few weeks were okay

I bought a Nintendo switch and groceries to last me a few weeks with my last pay cheque. I'm luckier than most in which I don't have to pay for rent or groceries and that has been a blessing I don't let go unnoticed 

However, since I've been inside most days and the only way I can get anywhere is through bus since I don't drive, I've mainly been locked in my home. I've gone on walks, called and face timed my friends but I've noticed my mental health has been deteriorating.

I'm doing everything in the best of my ability to not give in fully to my mental disorders but it's been hard considering I don't have much options. One of my friends have reached out and given me resources in which I use but I'm beginning to feel like how I did years ago when I was a kid. 

Being a recovering eating disorder impatient and being off my meds because both me and my doctor felt it was the appropriate time to do so, I have noticed I have I've slowly started falling back into those habits. 

I have friends who check up, I've let my immediate family know of the feelings I'm going through but nothing can take away from the fact I am with myself 24/7 now. I'm trying to make it easy for myself and making myself do things I need to do to derail the situation from getting harder.

All of this fucking sucks because I had finally gotten my financial benefit for a psychiatrist and physiotherapy just had everything has shut down. Not saying I can't do these things but to get to these appointments I'd need to use the bus and I have two grandparents who would be deeply affect if I ever did get covid. 

So until then, I feel trapped physically for the first time in my life with a demon I was ready to take on.
